spec: DATA_MODEL.md §18 module 13 — workspaces (the default 4-panel WEI / TOP / GP SPX / W "Core" per user, 7 rows), watchlists MAG7 / "S&P 500 Top 25" / Core, portfolio "Demo Long" with 12 lots and positions.
layoutNote: `layout` is API.md §5.7's WorkspaceLayout and seed/workspaces.ts parses it with the wire schema (@terminal/sdk/wire/rest/workspaces) before writing, so a layout this fixture gets wrong is a seed failure rather than a 500 on somebody's first morning — the same guarantee http/routes/workspaces.ts gives DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_LAYOUT at module load.
panelNote: The W panel names its list as `{ watchlist: { name: 'Core' } }`. W's own param schema accepts a name reference as well as an id (packages/core/src/functions/manifests/W.ts#WWatchlistRef), so the layout needs no id substitution and stays valid whatever `watchlist_id` the sequence hands out — which also means a layout written into bloomberg_dev is still correct after a reset.
gpRangeNote: A STATED DEVIATION FROM §18, and the one number in this file chosen by measurement rather than by copying the spec. §18 module 13 names the panel `GP SPX` and does not fix its range; this fixture asked for `1Y`, and no daily range can draw it: `bars_daily` holds AAPL (1,255 closes) and nine FX pairs with a single row each and NO index at all, so the first chart every seeded user ever saw was an empty canvas with an honest `primary: NO_SOURCE — no bars in window` beside it, and `packages/e2e/tests/smoke.spec.ts` carried a `test.fail` saying so. The only SPX history the universe has is `yahoo-chart-SPX-5d-5m.json` — 376 five-minute bars from 2026-09-09 09:30 to 2026-09-15 14:45 New York — and GP reaches intraday bars only at `1D` and `5D` (its own help text says so). Measured over the seeded database: `POST /functions/GP/run {security:{ref:'SPX Index'},params:{range:'5D'}}` answers 200 with `window.periodicity '5m'` and `window.bars 376`, where `1D`, `1M` and `1Y` each answer 200 with zero bars and `primary NO_SOURCE`. So the panel keeps its instrument — which is what §18 specifies — and gains a plot. Note for whoever seeds index history: `1D` wants ONE-minute bars and SPX has none, so even once `R` works, cycling down to 1D finds nothing; that is a capture, not a fixture. AND `R` DOES NOT WORK TODAY, which an earlier version of this note offered as the way off 5D. GP's manifest declares `{ key: 'R', action: 'cycle-range' }` (GP.ts L385) and nothing consumes the action: `App.tsx#screenAction` answers `NOT_APPLICABLE: cycle-range: this key is declared by the screen but not wired yet` (L1442-1444, a gap BUILD_STATUS.md records), and the range chips beside the chart carry `press R to cycle to 1M` as a title regardless (GP/Screen.tsx L196). So the only way to another range is to type one, and the form is POSITIONAL: `SPX Index GP 1M <GO>`. `RANGE=1M` is refused — `GP.paramGrammar` lists `range` as its first positional slot and its `keyed` map holds TYPE/ADJ/VS/CCY/NORM/PER/LOG and no RANGE, so `parseArgs` answers `ARG_PARSE: RANGE is not an argument of this function` (verified against the shipped grammar: `['5D']` parses to `range: '5D'` with no problems, `['RANGE=5D']` parses to nothing with that problem). Which is why this panel's `history` entry below reads `SPX Index GP 5D` and not `SPX Index GP RANGE=5D`: a history entry exists to be recalled and run, and the keyed form cannot be. The same un-runnable `RANGE=` spelling is still written by `functions/MSG`'s chart click-through (`MSG.default.json` holds `AAPL US Equity GP RANGE=1Y`) and is recorded in BUILD_STATUS.md rather than fixed from a seed fixture. IT DOES NOT EXPIRE, AND THAT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. `GP/resolve.ts#planWindow` plans a ROLLING calendar window off the as-of clock, so on 2026-10-01 a 5D window is 2026-09-24 → 2026-10-01 and contains none of the capture — which would make this fixture rot a week after it was written if that window were where the bars came from. It is not: the intraday read is `data/intraday.ts#recentSessions`, which takes the last `days` session DATES THAT HAVE BARS on or before the as-of date (`ORDER BY d DESC LIMIT 5`), the unit §GIP step 2 defines. The panel finds the capture's last five sessions however far in the past they are. The consequence worth knowing is that the `Window` kv row prints the PLANNED window and not the served one: measured on screen, `Window 2026-09-24 → 2026-10-01` over bars from 2026-09-09 to 2026-09-15, beside `Bars 376`, `High 7,676.27`, `Low 7,575.58`, `Periodicity 5m`. That is §GP's own shape (step 1 plans the window from the range, step 2 reads whole sessions) and it is visible only on a frozen replay universe; it lives in `functions/GP/resolve.ts`, not here. RETARGETING THE PANEL AT AAPL was the other candidate and was rejected, but NOT for the reason the old `test.fail` gave. That reason is gone, and it was re-measured in Chrome on the seeded desk before this fixture was touched: `W · Core` sends `{"s":"q:37367","f":["CHG_PCT_1D","PX_LAST"]}` for its SPX row, WEI widens the SAME subject to `["CHG_NET_1D","CHG_PCT_1D","PX_LAST","SESSION_STATE"]`, and Apple's row still reads `▼ -0.84%` — `SubscriptionManager#desiredFields` unions across holders in the shipped app, which is what `live-grid.spec.ts`' per-row field assertion also checks. At `5D` the question does not even arise: GP's intraday `LiveSpec` names `b1m:37367`, a different subject from any grid's, so the chart cannot replace a quote's field mask at all. What rejected the retarget is that it would rename the seeded panel that `panels.spec.ts` L89/L169, `layout-geometry.spec.ts` L133 and `export.spec.ts` L55 each assert on by name — and an index is what the default desk's chart is for.
gpNote: The GP panel's `security` is resolved at seed time from ticker `SPX` on exch_code `INDEX`. When seed/universe.ts has not run, no such instrument exists; the panel is then written with `security: null` and a warning, because REF-01 forbids carrying a bare ticker in a frame and a frame that names an instrument id nothing resolves to is worse than a frame with none.
watchlistNote: Every list is `shared_scope: 'firm'` and owned by a Demo Capital user, which is what makes the tenant-isolation assertion meaningful: a firm-shared list is the widest scope a watchlist has, and Other Desk must still not see it (FUNCTIONS_TIER1 W.rls.test.ts, PORT-07/SEC-05). `watchlists.name` is unique per owner, so the three lists are owned by two different users only where that reads naturally.

watchlists.name: Core
watchlists.itemsNote: Cross-asset on purpose — an equity, an index, a G10 pair and a benchmark govt — so that the monitor's per-asset-class field resolution is exercised by the default screen rather than only by a test. The last row is a CHRT-07 formula row, which is the one watchlist_items shape whose instrument_id is NULL.

watchlists.name: S&P 500 Top 25
watchlists.derivedNote: The members are NOT listed here. "Top 25" is an ordering by index weight and the weights are a recorded fact — the SPY N-PORT and SSGA holdings files that seed/universe.ts writes into etf_holdings — so the list is built by reading the latest as_of_date for SPY and taking the 25 largest weights. Hand-copying 25 tickers would put a stale, unprovenanced ranking in a fixture; reading the holdings means the list is whatever the recorded file says. When etf_holdings is empty the watchlist is created with no items and a warning, because an empty list is visibly empty whereas a guessed one is not.

portfolioNote: `lots` and `positions` carry no provenance_id column: they are the user's own book, source `internal.user`, and this fixture IS their source (DATA_MODEL §19 — confidential, not personal data, RLS-isolated by firm). Quantities and costs are curated demo values, which is why they sit in fixtures/seed rather than being derived from a capture. `as_of_date` is the recorded world's date, 2026-09-15, so PORT values against the seeded bars_daily instead of against a date no bar exists for.
